_note: Courier contracts and reputation. Boards refresh every refresh_days per port. Each job allows a window from when it is taken: a reference ship's quick plan (a stock Mule at full tanks, or a long-haul refit) x slack, so a light, fast, direct trip makes it and a laden one may not. Pay = (pay_base + pay_per_day x trip days) x (1 + urgency x (slack_max - slack)) x kind/channel multipliers; passengers pay per head. Reputation is per operator (the client); tiers gate premium jobs and approaches. Lateness pays late_fraction and costs reputation; past fail_after x the window the contract fails.

covert._note: Secret work (sim/systems/contract_system.gd), unlocked at unlock_rep standing with any operator (Reliable). Covert jobs come only as approaches, chance of the time once unlocked. Each has a watcher (an operator whose ports would stop you). While carrying one, every second a watcher's port sees the ship builds suspicion: transponder_mult as fast with the transponder on, filed_mult as fast on a trip with a filed plan (they know where you are going). On a trip without a plan, losing every port's sensors loses them too: suspicion resets. At suspicion_s you are caught, as you are docking at a watcher's port with covert work aboard: the job fails, caught_fine_cr, caught_rep with the watcher and client_rep with the client, and an offence. impound_after offences and the ship is held at your next port until you pay impound_fee_cr. Listening devices and spy satellites go in on a long, slow drift from within plant_m of their target, coasting, dark and unseen by it; ordinary satellites anywhere within release_m of their orbit (or from the bay at the port). Free departures (no plan filed) unlock with secret work; leaving a busy_port that way costs unfiled_fine_cr and unfiled_rep with its operator, more each time (unfiled_repeat_mult): traffic control remembers.
openers: A note slipped under your cabin door: a time, a berth number, and no name.
The bartender sets down a drink you didn't order. 'From the gentleman who has already left.'
Your co-pilot finds a message hidden in a routine traffic bulletin. It knows your ship's name.
A dockhand helping with your lines says, very quietly, that someone would like a word.
Someone has left a message at the dock office, marked for you by name.
A woman in a Commons jacket finds you at the bar. 'You're the one who got the vaccines through. We have something.'
The harbourmaster catches you before you're through the lock. 'There's a client asking for you specifically.'
Your co-pilot flags a private channel request. Encrypted, polite, and well paid.

_hand_note: hand_items are small enough to carry in the cabin (letters, papers, a briefcase, data): they take no hold space, only their own few kilograms of mass (hand_mass_t). Passengers ride in berths and take no hold space either.
